text: What if someone is following you down a dark alley?
Imagine walking home late at night.
The streets are almost empty.
There are barely any cars,
and the only sound you can hear is your own footsteps.
But then, you notice something strange.
Someone is walking behind you.
You turn right.
He turns right.
You cross the street.
He crosses the street too.
You stop in front of a shop window,
pretending to look at something.
And in the reflection, you see him.
A tall man wearing a black jacket.
He is standing just a few meters behind you.
And he is looking directly at you.
You tell yourself it's probably just a coincidence.
But then he starts getting closer.
And when you take out your phone to call someone,
he takes out his too.
But this story actually started 20 minutes earlier.
You were walking home after meeting a friend.
It was already late,
and there were almost no buses left.
So you decided to walk.
You knew this neighborhood well.
You had walked these streets hundreds of times.
Nothing had ever happened before.
At first, you heard ordinary footsteps behind you.
You didn't think much of it.
But after a few minutes, you realize something.
The footsteps never disappeared.
You walked faster.
He walked faster too.
You stopped near a shop and checked your phone.
Through the reflection in the window,
you saw him again.
He was standing about 10 meters away.
Now you were sure someone was following you.
You decided to take a different route.
You turned into a narrow alley,
hoping he would continue down the main street.
But a few seconds later, you heard the same footsteps.
He had followed you.
The alley was much darker than you remembered.
Old garages stood on one side.
Tall apartment walls stood on the other.
The streetlights barely reached the ground.
You took out your phone.
You wanted to call your friend.
But before you could press the call button,
you heard a voice.
Hey, wait.
You didn't turn around.
I'm talking to you.
The voice was much closer now.
You started walking faster.
The exit was just ahead.
You could already see the lights of the main street.
Then your phone vibrated.
A message appeared from an unknown number.
It said, don't turn around, run.
You froze.
Who sent that message?
And how did they know what was happening?
You slowly turned around.
The man was standing only a few steps away.
He was tall, broad-shouldered, and wearing a black jacket.
His face was hidden in the darkness.
Finally stopped, he said quietly.
You asked him what he wanted.
He didn't answer.
Instead, he took out his phone and showed you the screen.
There was a photograph of you.
It had been taken earlier that evening.
You were standing right outside the shop
where you had first noticed him.
Where did you get that?
You asked.
The man slowly put his phone away.
You'd better stop asking questions.
Suddenly, you noticed movement near the exit.
Another person was standing there.
He wasn't moving.
He was just watching you.
Now there were two strangers between you
and the main street.
You stepped backward.
The first man stepped forward.
Then, suddenly, a loud noise came from somewhere behind him.
A door slammed.
For a moment, headlights from a passing car
lit up the entire alley.
You used that moment to move toward the brighter street.
The strangers didn't grab you.
They simply watched as you walked away.
When you finally reached the main road,
you saw a 24-hour convenience store.
There was a shopkeeper inside.
Next to it was a guarded parking lot
with a security guard standing near the entrance.
You quickly took out your phone to call for help.
But before you could dial, another message appeared.
You chose the wrong place.
You looked up.
Across the street stood the same man in the black jacket.
He smiled.
Then he slowly raised his phone.
On the screen was another photograph of you.
But this time, someone else was standing
right next to you.
You looked around.
There was nobody there.
And that's when you realize something.
Maybe the danger had been much closer
than you ever imagined.
Now, you have two choices.
Option A, enter the convenience store,
tell the shopkeeper what happened,
and ask them to call the police.
Option B, go to the guarded parking lot
and ask the security guard for help.
What would you choose?
Comment A or B below.
Your choice will decide what happens in the next episode.
